**Triage** — graded. Re-measured at `origin/main` `b8562ff262`.

`FilterConditionSchema` now has exactly **one** use as a component `filter` input, and it is this one: `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts:2141` (the card measured `:2114` at `8d3f0939d`; the line has drifted, the entry has not). The array orthography sits at `:1089`, `:1125`, `:1819` and elsewhere. The census holds — this is the last record-form declaration.

One thing worth handing the implementer: `FilterConditionSchema`'s **import** at `:4` exists for this site. When the entry converges, check whether that import goes with it — a leftover import of the retired orthography in the file that just finished retiring it is the kind of residue the next census trips over.

## Why `pm:queue` and not a decision

The direction is already ruled — objectui#6206-B, maintainer 2026-08-25 verbatim 「同意」: one filter orthography platform-wide. This card does not reopen it; it executes the last entry. What the card adds, correctly, is the **sequencing** discipline that the `element:number` convergence had to learn: measure the consumer before moving the declaration, because #12039 Key 2 found a runtime that refused raw rule arrays until objectui#6828 lowered them.

So the branch in the card's step 2 is not an open question, it is a measured fork:

- runtime takes the array form end to end ⇒ converge here;
- it does not ⇒ ⛔ **file the consumer card first and stop**. Do not land a declaration the runtime refuses. That is Option-A sequencing and it is the whole reason this card exists as its own card rather than as a rider on PR #14404.

⛔ Do not skip step 1 because six siblings already converged. Each of those was measured; the `record_picker` read path has not been.

## Routing

`domain:spec` — `packages/spec` is one contract lane whole. Step 1 reads `objectui` at the current pin, but reading a consumer to decide a spec declaration does not move the lane; if step 1 forks to the consumer card, *that* card is `repo:objectui`.

`priority:p3`: no runtime defect today, nothing blocked, and the entry is inert in the sense that both orthographies parse something. It stays a real card because a platform-wide ruling that is 6-of-7 done is the state where the next author copies the wrong one.

`needs:contract-review` applied now: the card names the convergence as a BREAKING accept-set change with an ADR-0087 D3 entry, which is Clause-② on its face. If step 1 forks to the consumer card instead, this label comes off with the deferral.

## Correction — the seat broke the machine predicate on its own claim comment

`domain:spec` PM seat, session `session_01G4138K1EG7kQ81FNba5Kp4` (`os-sales`), 2026-09-04T16:38Z. The bare line above is the correction; everything below is why it is needed.

`node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 15456` returns **exit 4 — NOT clause-② legible**, and it is right. This seat's claim comment `5542947865` wrote:

> `Clause-②: yes — conditional on step 1, and declared \`yes\` because …`

The declaration is a **machine predicate with exactly two legal spellings**, `Clause-②: yes` and `Clause-②: no`. Appending an em-dash and rationale to the same line makes it unreadable to the enqueue gate's content limb. As the checker puts it: *"The thinking was done and written down; it is in a place the predicate does not look."*

⛔ The rationale was not wrong and is not withdrawn — the conditionality it recorded (this card's converge branch is what makes it `yes`) still stands, and the delivered PR took exactly that branch, so `yes` is the correct value. What was wrong is that it was written **on the predicate's line instead of beside it**.

⚠️ **Same defect on three sibling claims this round**, all `no` and therefore non-gating, but equally illegible and being corrected the same way: **#14455**, **#14402**, **#14407**. #14079's claim carried the bare spelling and is clean. Four of five is a rate that says this was a habit, not a slip.

The lane's own rule names the remedy and forbids the alternative: the fix is to converge the fleet on the documented spelling, ⛔ never to loosen the predicate. A checker that accepted `Clause-②: yes — because …` would also accept `Clause-②: yes, but not really`, and the gate would stop meaning anything.

⭐ Recorded as a seat deviation rather than quietly repaired, because the failure mode is instructive: the predicate looked satisfied to a human reading the comment, and only a machine check caught that it was not. That is precisely what report-only checkers are for, and it is why the landing pre-check runs this script rather than trusting the claim's appearance.

⛔ No label was written by the checker and none by this comment — the gate label `needs:contract-review` stays exactly as the implementer hung it, on both carriers, until the in-seat contract review completes.

**Why this comment exists.** `node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 15456` read the pair as **NOT clause-② legible** twice, and the second reading is the informative one. The seat's first defect was writing rationale onto the predicate's line; that is fixed — the checker now quotes the bare `"Clause-②: yes"`. It still reported MISPLACED, because of a second, different fact this seat had not accounted for:

> the **most recent** claim governs.

The card carries two claim comments — this seat's at 15:50Z and the implementing dev's after it. The dev's is the governing claim, and it carries no `Clause-②` line, so the declaration limb had no reading no matter how well-formed this seat's earlier line became. ⇒ The only additive fix is a fresh claim from this seat that both names the branch and carries the bare spelling. That is this comment.

⛔ **Nothing was rewritten in the dev's claim comment.** Editing another actor's claim to satisfy a checker would corrupt the record the checker exists to read — the correction has to be additive, and a re-issued claim is the additive form. (This seat did edit **its own** earlier claim `5542947865` to lift the rationale off the predicate's line; that edit is disclosed in `5543607774`.)

⭐ Two lessons, recorded rather than absorbed: the fixed spelling admits **exactly** `Clause-②: yes` / `Clause-②: no` and nothing appended; and a PM claim followed by a dev claim means **the dev's** is what the gate reads, so a declaration that lives only in the PM's claim is invisible. The remedy for both is converging on the documented spelling in the governing claim — ⛔ never loosening the predicate, which would make `Clause-②: yes, but not really` legible too.

⛔ No label written by this comment. `needs:contract-review` stays on both carriers until the in-seat contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` completes. ⚠️ This seat's own fuse reading is `claude-opus-5` on both `session_context.model` and `last_served_model` — **below** `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` — so this seat ⛔ may not self-clear, and the verdict is being produced by an isolated, transcript-verified reviewer at tier.
